# 🫥 NoMount Suite Loads root modules without mounting anything, RRO overlays included. No `overlayfs`, no `tmpfs`: the **Prism** kernel engine redirects VFS lookups, so nothing shows up in `/proc/mounts`. It is a metamodule. > **Beta.** Reports from other phones, managers and odd modules move it to > stable. `nomount export` builds the bundle, hide list redacted.
Status Hiding Rules Checks Duck Detector
## Install Each [release](https://github.com/Bouteillepleine/NoMount-Suite/releases/latest) has two zips: | Zip | For | | :--- | :--- | | `00_NoMount-Module` | A kernel with the engine built in: the [`BakaSu`](https://github.com/Bouteillepleine/OnePlus-BakaSu_NMS/releases), [`KsuNext`](https://github.com/Bouteillepleine/OnePlus-KsuNext_NMS/releases) or [`SukiSu`](https://github.com/Bouteillepleine/OnePlus-SukiSu_NMS/releases) OnePlus kernels, or your own build with `CONFIG_NOMOUNT=y` from [`hookless/`](hookless/) | | `01_NoMount-Module-LKM` | A stock GKI kernel. It loads the engine as a module at boot (android12-5.10 to android17-6.18) | Flash it from your manager, reboot, then check from a root shell: ```sh alias nomount=/data/adb/modules/meta-nomount/bin/arm64-v8a/nomount nomount check # want: verdict: clean, 0 failed, 0 unmeasured ``` Needs arm64 and KernelSU (or a fork) or Magisk. SUSFS is not needed. Updates are the same flash and keep your settings. ## Safe Guard boot Let it boot twice more: after three failed boots the Suite parks itself. To park it by hand from recovery: ```sh mkdir -p /data/adb/nomount && touch /data/adb/nomount/disabled ``` ## Commands The WebUI does all of this. From a shell: `nomount check`, `reload`, `uid block `, `whiteout add `, `export`. `nomount --help` has the rest. To report a problem, attach what **Checks → Developer tools → Export** writes. ## Building ```sh cargo test && ANDROID_NDK_HOME=/path/to/ndk scripts/package.sh --build --version vX.Y.Z ``` ## License and credits GPL-3.0, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). A rewrite of **[maxsteeel/nomount](https://github.com/maxsteeel/nomount)**. Thanks to [HymoFS](https://github.com/Anatdx/HymoFS), [A7mdwassa](https://github.com/A7mdwassa), [ZQZCC](https://github.com/ZQZCC), [backslashxx](https://github.com/backslashxx), [KernelSU](https://github.com/tiann/KernelSU), SukiSU-Ultra, [SUSFS](https://gitlab.com/simonpunk/susfs4ksu) and every tester. Modifying a kernel can brick a phone or lose data. Use at your own risk.
readmeHTML:
🫥 NoMount Suite

Loads root modules without mounting anything, RRO overlays included. No

overlayfs, no tmpfs: the Prism kernel engine redirects VFS lookups, so

nothing shows up in /proc/mounts. It is a metamodule.

> Beta. Reports from other phones, managers and odd modules move it to

> stable. nomount export builds the bundle, hide list redacted.

Status Hiding Rules Checks Duck Detector

Install

Each release has two zips:

| Zip | For |

| :--- | :--- |

| 00_NoMount-Module | A kernel with the engine built in: the BakaSu, KsuNext or SukiSu OnePlus kernels, or your own build with CONFIG_NOMOUNT=y from hookless/ |

| 01_NoMount-Module-LKM | A stock GKI kernel. It loads the engine as a module at boot (android12-5.10 to android17-6.18) |

Flash it from your manager, reboot, then check from a root shell:

alias nomount=/data/adb/modules/meta-nomount/bin/arm64-v8a/nomount
nomount check      # want: verdict: clean, 0 failed, 0 unmeasured

Needs arm64 and KernelSU (or a fork) or Magisk. SUSFS is not needed. Updates

are the same flash and keep your settings.

Safe Guard boot

Let it boot twice more: after three failed boots the Suite parks itself. To

park it by hand from recovery:

mkdir -p /data/adb/nomount && touch /data/adb/nomount/disabled

Commands

The WebUI does all of this. From a shell: nomount check, reload,

uid block , whiteout add , export. nomount --help has the

rest. To report a problem, attach what Checks → Developer tools → Export

writes.

Building

cargo test && ANDROID_NDK_HOME=/path/to/ndk scripts/package.sh --build --version vX.Y.Z

License and credits

GPL-3.0, see LICENSE. A rewrite of

maxsteeel/nomount. Thanks to

HymoFS, A7mdwassa,

ZQZCC, backslashxx,

KernelSU, SukiSU-Ultra,

SUSFS and every tester.

Modifying a kernel can brick a phone or lose data. Use at your own risk.
